headline: High-risk overlap: both agents have broad network and MCP access, while nullclaw can write/modify state and next-ai-draw-io can ingest files and browser content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs, text, images, and draw.io XML and uses MCP/browser tooling; nullclaw can also use MCP and browser/web fetch. That creates a plausible instruction-injection path if content from A is fed into B or vice versa, though no shared channel is explicitly documented. The pathway is inferred from documented surfaces, not observed behavior.
conditions: IF outputs from next-ai-draw-io are copied into nullclaw prompts or webhooks, injected instructions can be acted on.
IF either agent treats imported document text as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes viable.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of generated text into downstream prompts.
Add a manual review step before passing A outputs to B.
Strip instruction-like markup from imported documents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent content.
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted prompt templates for MCP/webhook inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch sensitive material: next-ai-draw-io handles API keys and environment variables, while nullclaw handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and workspace files. Both also have broad network egress and MCP/browser surfaces, so sensitive content can leave the local workspace by default if either agent forwards context to external models or services. The blast radius includes secrets exfiltration.
conditions: IF either agent forwards full context or file contents to a third-party model/API, secrets may be exposed.
IF both agents share the same workspace or credentials, one agent can read data the other processes.
mitigations: Separate credentials and workspaces for each agent.
Rotate any API keys used by either agent.
Disable network egress for test runs.
Review logs for secret-bearing prompts or uploads.
requires-engineering: add secret redaction before any outbound request.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; next-ai-draw-io can run browsers and use MCP, and both support multiple instances. If they operate on the same workspace or repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and corrupt state. The profiles do not show locking or isolation between them, so the conflict is plausible in default shared-workspace deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or workspace, concurrent edits can collide.
IF nullclaw commits while next-ai-draw-io rewrites files, git state can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use a git lock or serialized commit queue.
Review diffs before any commit.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and nullclaw has delegate/schedule/webhook-style automation surfaces. If B consumes A's generated diagrams or extracted facts without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions. This is not proven by direct integration, but the documented toolchains make the pathway credible.
conditions: IF nullclaw uses next-ai-draw-io output as authoritative input, downstream actions may reflect A's mistakes.
IF A-generated content is routed into B's webhook or scheduling flows without review, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B acts.
Mark A outputs as untrusted in prompts.
Add a verification checklist for facts and citations.
Limit B automation to read-only dry runs.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before action execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and unverified, but they touch different sensitive classes and have different storage surfaces. next-ai-draw-io requests environment variables and handles API keys; nullclaw stores workspace files, audit logs, and multiple token types under ~/.nullclaw/workspace and config paths. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch for secrets and logs, though no specific jurisdictional mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent's workspace or logs, retention obligations may diverge.
IF secrets are stored in ~/.nullclaw/workspace while next-ai-draw-io forwards them to external APIs, compliance controls may fail.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either workspace.
Review retention settings for logs and audit trails.
Separate secret storage from document-processing inputs.
Delete temporary files after each session.
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency boundaries.
